title: Head of Risk and Money Services at Gusto
description:
About Gusto 

 At Gusto, we’re on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. 

 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy. 

 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. 

 Head of Risk & Money Services 

 At Gusto, we help more than 500,000 small businesses create great places to work for their people. We do this through modern payroll, employee benefits, expert HR, and financial services. 

 We are searching for a seasoned financial services operator and regulated-domain leader to own one of Gusto’s most consequential customer-facing functions: Risk & Money Services. This role sits within CX and Gusto’s Financial Services organization and reports directly to the Head of Financial Services. 

 Every dollar that moves through Gusto’s platform — payroll being delivered on time, wages being deposited into Gusto Wallet, cash advances being issued, disputes being resolved — carries real financial and regulatory weight. Risk & Money Services is the team that protects this trust at the most critical edges of money movement: fraud and payment risk decisioning, Reg E dispute operations, collections, and the consumer money products that sit at the intersection of and its small business mission. 

 This function spans three interconnected practices: 

 
 Risk Operations — fraud ops, account takeover detection, payment-risk decisioning, and collections across both employer and employee money movement. This team makes real-time, high-stakes decisions on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, BSA/AML compliance, whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time, and whether a fraud signal warrants action. The financial impact of individual calls is material. Focusing on risk mitigation and exceptional service is no easy task 
 Dispute Operations — Reg E dispute processing across Gusto’s banking and money-movement products, from intake through resolution and provisional credit decisioning. This team owns Gusto’s most regulated customer-facing process and operates at the intersection of customer trust and regulatory obligation. 
 Money Services and Banking — the operational home for Gusto Wallet, Cash Advance, and Gusto’s expanding consumer financial products. This team is responsible for building the operational infrastructure that supports Gusto’s growth in consumer banking — while protecting the customers who depend on it. 
 

 You will lead this organization through a senior leadership team, who carry full ownership for their function’s outcomes, not just execution within it.Partner deeply with Compliance, Legal, Engineering, and Product across Gusto’s products, and serve as the operational owner of the functions that sit at the regulated edge of Gusto’s financial platform 

 This is a builder’s role. Risk & Money Services is being stood up as a defined function within a new domain — you will set the SLAs, design the controls, build the metrics framework, establish the governance, and create the playbook that lets Gusto move money with confidence and scale. 

 Our mission is to create a world where work empowers a better life, and it starts right here at Gusto. That’s why we’re committed to building a collaborative and inclusive workplace, both physically and virtually. 

 Here’s what you’ll do 

 
 Own Risk & Money Services end to end. Be the single accountable leader for fraud and payment risk decisioning, BSA/AML compliance, Reg E dispute operations, collections, and the operational backbone of Gusto’s money products. Own the customer experience, the regulatory posture, and the financial outcomes across this entire function. 
 Lead a multi-disciplinary regulated financial services organization through leaders who lead. Direct an organization spanning risk operations, dispute and fraud operations, and consumer money — through leaders who own their function end to end, whom you’ll continue to develop, hire, and scale. Be the keeper of quality, speed, and regulatory integrity across all three practices. 
 Stand up Risk & Money Services as a defined operational function. Define the governance, the metrics framework, the SLAs, and the reporting infrastructure for a function that is being formalized for the first time. Build the operating muscle — controls documentation, audit readiness, workforce management, and escalation frameworks — that makes this domain run with the reliability a regulated function requires. 
 Own the highest-stakes real-time financial decisions in Gusto’s customer operations. Be accountable for the decisions your team makes every day on whether payroll goes out when something looks wrong, whether a dispute warrants provisional credit, whether a fraud signal warrants action, and whether a fund recovery effort can be executed in time. These decisions carry material financial impact for customers and for Gusto — and they happen in real time. 
 Own Gusto’s Reg E compliance posture at the operational level. Lead the operational program that governs Gusto’s Reg E dispute obligations — intake, investigation, provisional credit, resolution, and customer communication — in partnership with Compliance and Legal. Ensure the team’s practices are auditable, scalable, and consistently defensible. 
 Lead BSA/AML operational response. Own the customer-facing operational work triggered by BSA/AML alert activity — transaction monitoring response, customer outreach, account action — in partnership with Gusto’s Compliance program. Ensure operational response meets the timeliness and documentation standards required by Gusto’s sponsor bank relationships and regulatory obligations. 
 Build Consumer Money for growth. Own the operational infrastructure for Gusto Wallet, Cash Advance, and Gusto’s expanding consumer financial product suite. Build the SOPs, workforce model, controls, and SLAs that support consumer product growth while protecting the customers who depend on these products. 
 Drive AI-native transformation in a regulated financial domain. Partner with Gusto’s shared service platform and AI organization to bring AI agents, semantic knowledge, and automation capabilities into Risk & Money Services — accelerating fraud decisioning speed, dispute throughput, and risk signal accuracy while protecting the regulatory accountability this domain requires. 
 Be the operational counterpart to Product, Engineering, and Risk partners. Operate as the direct customer experience and operational owner across Gusto’s money and risk product organizations — translating the operational and regulatory reality of risk and money movement into product priorities, and translating product roadmap into operational and regulatory readiness. 
 Represent Risk & Money Services externally. Be the direct voice with Gusto’s sponsor bank partners, regulators, and auditors on matters affecting risk and money movement — not just the internal operator of the controls they require, but the leader they know and deal with directly. 
 Build the playbook for new financial products. Establish Risk & Money Services as the operational home for the risk and money movement functions of Gusto’s growing financial product portfolio — including business banking expansion, new money services, and future consumer financial products — with the controls and operational readiness already in place. 
 Bring out the best in your people. Care deeply about the Gusties on your team. Help them do the best work of their careers, grow into bigger versions of themselves, and feel proud of building a risk and money function that protects Gusto’s customers and the business at the same time. 
 

 Here’s what we’re looking for 

 
 12+ years of industry experience leading financial services operations in banking, payments, money movement, fraud and risk, or related regulated domains — with demonstrated depth in the mechanics of how money moves, where it fails, and how regulated institutions respond. 
 7+ years as a departmental leader running large, multi-disciplinary financial services operations teams — with experience managing through senior direct reports across distinct operational functions. 
 Deep expertise in banking and money movement operations — including Reg E dispute processing, BSA/AML operational response, ACH and real-time payments risk, sponsor bank operational requirements, and the controls infrastructure that makes regulated money movement auditable. 
 Hands-on background in fraud and payment risk — experience building or leading fraud operations that make real-time decisioning calls with material financial consequences, including payment risk scoring, account takeover response, and fund recovery operations. 
 Experience in consumer financial products — operational background in consumer banking, digital wallet, cash advance, or similar products, including the SOPs, customer communications frameworks, and compliance controls these products require. 
 Track record of standing up or formalizing regulated financial functions — building the SLAs, controls documentation, governance, and reporting infrastructure that make regulated work auditable, scalable, and defensible under examination. 
 Demonstrated experience navigating sponsor bank and regulatory relationships — understanding how to operate within the constraints of a bank partnership, including audit readiness, operational policy alignment, and escalation to compliance and legal. 
 Track record of leading through high-stakes, real-time financial decisions where individual calls carry material financial cost to customers or to the business. 
 Experience building reliable, scalable, AI-native operations in regulated domains — with the judgment to know where automation accelerates and where regulatory accountability stays non-negotiable. 
 Strong cross-functional muscle with Product, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, and Risk — particularly in fintech, banking, or financial product environments where operational leaders must drive product decisions, not just react to them. 
 Track record of delivering on the diverse needs of multiple senior partners across overlapping financial product lines. 
 Demonstrated ability to lead through significant organizational change — bringing teams along with clarity, candor, and consistency during periods of high operational flux. 
 Empathetic and employee-focused: you care deeply about the people on your team, you help them achieve their personal and professional goals, and you enable them to do the best work of their lives. 
 Track record of building diverse and inclusive teams. 
 

 Our cash compensation range for this role is $170,000 to 215,000 per year in Denver. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above. 

 Ou

title: Senior L&D Specialist at Gusto
description:
About Gusto 

 At Gusto, we’re on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. 

 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy. 

 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. 

 About the Role: 

 Our CX Learning & Development team is dedicated to building an exceptional customer experience by equipping our CX professionals with the skills they need to thrive, and it all starts with creating impactful, data-driven learning experiences. We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Learning & Development Specialist to lead program design, facilitate learning in key areas, and manage stakeholder relationships to drive business success. The ideal candidate will have experience in robust course design, program management, and coaching, with a track record of delivering high-quality learning solutions in fast-paced environments. 

 About the Team: 

 This role is part of our Learning & Development team, within our Customer Experience organization. Our CX organization is the linchpin of our world-class experience. With their passion, insight, and customer advocacy, the CX team has helped Gusto maintain industry-leading NPS scores while serving over 500,000 customers. We strive to positively influence millions of businesses and hundreds of millions of employees across the country. 

 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 

 Facilitation 

 
 Facilitate in-person, virtual, and hybrid learning sessions across at least six distinct and complex knowledge areas, demonstrating a deep understanding of subject matter and the ability to tailor delivery for various audience levels, including mid & senior leadership participants. 
 Take the lead in creating an inclusive and dynamic learning environment that challenges participants to apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills in real-world scenarios. 
 Actively engage learners through interactive techniques, real-world examples, and structured activities that reinforce course content and objectives. 
 Provide feedback & coaching to learners in real-time, offering guidance and support to enhance their understanding and skills development. 
 Design and facilitate sessions that teach CX teams how to use AI tools responsibly and effectively in their daily workflows. 
 Leverage AI-assisted tools to enhance participation and personalization during live training. 
 Uses insights from AI-driven learning platforms to tailor discussions, provide targeted feedback, and reinforce learning outcomes. 
 

 Instructional Design & Communications 

 
 Lead comprehensive course design efforts, driving innovation and continuous improvement in learning materials and methods to ensure they meet the evolving needs of the CX team and broader business. 
 Take full ownership of content development, acting as the final point of quality control for course content updates and ensuring that all learning materials are aligned with strategic business goals. 
 Develop and manage high-level communication strategies for learning initiatives, collaborating with leadership and cross-functional teams to ensure alignment and stakeholder buy-in. 
 Integrate AI-enabled design approaches into curriculum development to improve personalization, scalability, and learner engagement. 
 Uses AI-enabled authoring tools to rapidly prototype, script, and iterate on training materials. 
 

 Program Management 

 
 Manage complex, high-visibility learning programs from end to end, with full accountability for program success, continuous improvement, and alignment with business outcomes. 
 Oversee multiple CX Academy cohorts simultaneously, ensuring efficient cohort management and providing strategic guidance on program implementation and learner success. 
 Monitor participant progress and engagement, proactively identifying and addressing potential barriers to success. 
 Identify and drive improvements across programs, utilizing feedback from participants and stakeholders to evolve learning offerings and ensure continued alignment with business goals. 
 Operationalize AI tools to automate repetitive program administration tasks where appropriate. 
 Implement AI-assisted project tracking, communication, and reporting tools to streamline coordination and status visibility. 
 

 Stakeholder Management 

 
 Serve as a primary contact for high-level stakeholders, developing and maintaining strategic relationships to ensure learning programs are aligned with business priorities. 
 Collaborate with senior leadership and department heads, providing expert consultation to design learning initiatives that directly support organizational growth and CX effectiveness. 
 Influence and negotiate with stakeholders at all levels, ensuring alignment between learning objectives and business needs, while also representing the voice of the CX L&D team in broader strategic discussions. 
 Use AI-supported data visualization and summary tools to synthesize stakeholder feedback and present actionable insights. 
 Communicates the value and limitations of AI-assisted solutions to stakeholders, ensuring transparency and alignment with organizational standards. 
 

 Data & Analytics 

 
 Own the learning data strategy for key programs, using sophisticated data analysis to assess program effectiveness, identify trends, and provide strategic insights to leadership. 
 Lead data-driven decision-making by tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) such as learner progress, program impact, and ROI, using this data to continuously optimize learning experiences. 
 Support other team members in developing their data analysis skills, helping them to understand and apply the Kirkpatrick Model of Training Evaluation data to their own work. 
 Leverage AI-derived insights to personalize learning and measure AI-enabled program effectiveness. 
 Leverages AI-powered analytics dashboards to identify learning trends, skill gaps, and opportunities for performance support. 
 Translates AI-derived insights into clear, actionable recommendations for program optimization. 
 

 Here’s what we’re looking for: 

 
 5+ years of L&D experience required 
 Ability to travel up to 50% of the time 
 Proactive, solution-oriented mindset with excellent organizational skills and attention to detail. 
 Adaptability and a passion for continuous learning and personal development in a fast-paced, dynamic environment. 
 Proven experience in learning program design, development, and facilitation across multiple knowledge areas. 
 Strong coaching skills, with the ability to mentor learners and participants as well as junior team members. 
 Expertise in managing end-to-end learning programs, including cohort management and continuous improvement. 
 Excellent stakeholder management skills, with a track record of building strong relationships and aligning learning initiatives with business goals. 
 Data-driven mindset, with the ability to analyze program outcomes and use insights for continuous enhancement. 
 Strategic thinker with a passion for driving business impact through learning and development. 
 Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment and manage multiple priorities effectively. 
 Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage and influence stakeholders at all levels. 
 ​​Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and evaluating AI-enabled learning solutions. 
 Demonstrated experimentation with AI applications in learning, communication, or content design. 
 Technical and AI-related skills:

 
 Practical experience with modern AI tools and workflows used in L&D. Familiarity with LLMs, prompt engineering, and APIs/integrations. 
 Familiarity with AI tools that support content creation, data analysis, or learner engagement. 
 Ability to prompt and fine-tune AI tools to produce high-quality, relevant, and brand-aligned outputs. 
 Skilled in balancing automation with human creativity, ensuring learning experiences remain empathetic and human-centered. 
 Experience evaluating or implementing AI-enabled learning platforms. 
 
 

 Our cash compensation amount for this role is $91,065/yr to $112,314/yr in Denver & most major metro locations, and $110,640/yr to $136,456/yr for San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above. 

 

 Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto’s subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale. 

 Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 

 When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees. 

 

 Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. 

 Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you. 

 Gusto takes security and protection of your personal information very seriously. Please review our Fraudulent Activity Disclaimer. 

 Personal information collected and processed as part of your Gusto application will be subject to Gusto’s Applicant Privacy Notice.

title: Backend Engineer at Catawiki
description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car, a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton, Lady Gaga’s Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe, we encounter exceptional objects every day. 

 We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts. 

 Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us. 

 
 Taking ownership and driving impact 
 Being open to change and feedback 
 Being passionate about our mission and our customers. 
 

 Your Mission 

 On our path to becoming the most visited online curated marketplace for special objects, our Engineering team is on a mission to deliver the best experience across our platforms by building best-in-class products for search and discovery, bidding, curation, logistics, payments, and support. 

 We’re a scale-up tackling customer-facing challenges at high scale, with 75,000 auctions per week and more than 10 million visitors per month. As a Backend Engineer , you’ll support one of our three verticals - Demand , Supply , or Fulfilment - improving and delivering product innovations for our platform. 

 Working in a small, fully autonomous, and highly collaborative Agile team, you will build scalable, maintainable, and resilient microservices and features. That’s why we’re looking for developers who share ideas, explore options, and communicate openly. 

 What You’ll Do 

 You’ll be part of a team with end-to-end responsibility for its own microservices, collaborating across disciplines to build, operate, and continuously improve our products. 

 
 Build end-to-end by designing, developing, testing, deploying, maintaining, and improving scalable microservices and features. 
 Own what you deliver , taking responsibility for the quality, resilience, and maintainability of your team’s services throughout their lifecycle. 
 Collaborate across disciplines while closely working with product designers, product owners, and frontend, backend, and mobile engineers to share ideas and deliver product innovations. 
 Improve how we work , identifying opportunities to make our engineering processes more effective and efficient. 
 Strengthen our engineering culture by documenting and advocating for development best practices across the team. 
 Raise product quality by fixing bugs and refactoring the codebase where necessary to keep our products reliable and maintainable. 
 Learn and experiment by testing new technologies and participating in Technical Week - a week dedicated to creativity, innovation, and knowledge sharing across domains after every two product sprints. 
 

 What You’ll Bring 

 You understand the full lifecycle of web development, identify opportunities, explore solutions, and keep customer needs at the center of your work. Our stack is mainly focused on Ruby; however, prior Ruby experience is not essential if you’re passionate about learning new things. 

 
 Strong software engineering foundations: 7+ years of software development experience, specifically with object-oriented programming. 
 Relevant product experience: 3+ years of experience working with customer-facing products in industries such as e-commerce, fintech, or SaaS. 
 Backend service expertise: Experience designing, implementing, and deploying backend services with a focus on high availability, low latency, and consistency. 
 API and data knowledge: A good understanding of API design, SQL, and relational databases. 
 Clear communication: Excellent English communication skills and comfort raising concerns, sharing ideas, and documenting your work. 
 Collaborative mindset: You contribute to the team, take initiative, and step in to help when needed. 
 Solution-oriented thinking: You actively identify opportunities and explore alternative approaches to solving problems. 
 Commitment to growth: You take ownership of developing your skills by learning new technologies and seeking new opportunities. 
 

 How We Work 

 Our engineers work in small, fully autonomous, and highly collaborative Agile teams aligned with one of three verticals: Demand, Supply, or Fulfilment. 

 
 Teams are responsible for their own microservices from design and development through deployment, maintenance, and improvement. 
 Engineers collaborate closely with product designers, product owners, and frontend, backend, and mobile colleagues. 
 We value bold thinking, curiosity, openness, initiative, and a strong customer focus. 
 Technical Week creates dedicated space for experimentation, creativity, innovation, and knowledge sharing across domains. 
 

 Where You’ll Be 

 This is a Hybrid role based in Lisbon. You will work from our Lisbon Office a minimum of 2 days per week. 

 In Return 

 You’ll be part of an enthusiastic, highly motivated team of 800+ Catawikians. 

 
 A competitive Annual Gross Base Salary depending on your level, competencies, and overall experience. 
 Meal Allowance Card stipend per working day, in addition to salary. 
 Health Insurance from day 1 (including dental coverage), with access to multiple hospitals and clinics and a vast wellness network. 
 A Work From Home Allowance to help with your monthly household bills. 
 Commuting between your home and our office is covered by Catawiki. 
 Amazing Office right in the centre of Lisbon. 
 

 Why You’ll Love Working with Us 

 
 Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business. 
 Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression. 
 A culture of connection defines us . We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work. 
 Celebrate life’s moments with us. You’ll receive a €100 Catavoucher when you join, a €50 Catavoucher on your birthday, and an extra day off each year to “Pursue Your Passion ” . We also offer additional leave for key work anniversaries and important life events. Benefits may vary by location. 
 

 Our Offices and Way of Working 

 Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based. 

 Interested? 

 Apply with an English CV and Cover Letter. By applying, you agree to Catawiki’s Applicant Privacy Policy. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

title: Junior Web Builder (Fully Remote, PH-Based Only, Fresh Grads Welcome to Apply) at Luxury Presence
description:
Luxury Presence is building the AI growth platform for real estate. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and other top investors, we’re a Series C company that has hit $100M in annual recurring revenue. More than 90,000 real estate professionals, including over 30% of the WSJ Real Trends top 100 agents in the United States, use us to run and grow their business. 

 Job Description 

 The Jr. Website Builder builds high-quality, high-performance real estate websites for the world’s leading agents on our proprietary Presence Platform, working within established templates. The role requires design intuition, technical proficiency (HTML/CSS), and a meticulous eye for detail to represent every client’s brand. 

 What You’ll Own 

 Website Design & Build 

 
 Build & Execution: Execute end-to-end builds of standard websites within established design frameworks on the Presence Platform, ensuring designs are visually compelling and fully responsive across devices. 

 Design Elevation: Apply cohesive color palettes and typography within established templates to reflect each client’s brand. 

 Review Project Requirements: Thoroughly review the project brief ticket, and all supporting materials before beginning any work to ensure a complete understanding of project requirements. 

 Client Translation Mastery: Understand and translate every client ask — from intake notes, discovery materials, and brand guidance — into the actual build. 

 User Experience: Design intuitive, engaging websites that provide an exceptional user experience and support lead generation. 
 

 Quality Assurance & Compliance 

 
 Rigorous Self-QA: Review and validate your work against the Build + Self-QA checklist before handoff. Quality is built throughout the work, not inspected at the end. 

 Compliance Checks: Verify state disclosure, brokerage branding rules, and MLS/IDX display requirements before any design work is considered done. 

 SEO Fundamentals: Apply SEO best practices, including meta-data optimization and link mapping. 
 

 Process & Communication 

 
 Task Management: Meet established handling time targets for website drafts and revisions while maintaining accurate task statuses to ensure clear workflow visibility and pipeline accuracy. 

 On-Time Ownership: Own the delivery timeline of your assigned builds, and resolve QA passbacks promptly so the project keeps moving. 

 Reporting: Escalate platform bugs, project blockers, and out-of-scope requests to your Team Lead in a timely manner. 

 Raise Risk Early: Communicate workload, dependency, or delivery risk before a deadline is missed — not after. 

 Communication: Maintain timely communication by responding within the same business day, acknowledging important instructions, and providing updates when working on time-sensitive or high-priority tasks. 
 

 What We’re Looking For 

 Experience 

 
 Little to no prior professional website-building experience required. 

 Prior exposure to block-based builders (e.g., Squarespace, Webflow, or similar) is a plus. 

 Fresh graduates with a strong portfolio and technical aptitude are strongly encouraged to apply — full training is provided. 
 

 Skills & Mindset 

 
 Technical: Foundational knowledge of HTML5, CSS, and JSON, with a willingness to build fluency quickly. Comfortable with Google Apps. 

 Design Eye: A developing sense of layout, balance, and aesthetic consistency. Knowledge in website UX/UI. 

 AI-Fluent: Comfortable using (or eager to learn) AI tools to accelerate coding and design tasks. 

 Coachable: Actively seeks feedback and applies it quickly. 

 Owner Mindset: Quick learner, reliable, strong work ethic — takes full responsibility for your work. 
 

 Core Values 

 
 Professionalism – Show up prepared, respectful, and dependable. 

 Ownership – Take responsibility for outcomes and follow through. 

 Communication – Be proactive, transparent, and timely. 

 Collaboration – Work well with others and contribute to team success. 

 Excellence – Deliver high-quality work with attention to detail. 

 Adaptability – Thrive in a fast-paced, remote environment. 

 Integrity – Do the right thing, even when no one is watching. Never mark QA notes or tasks complete before the work is actually implemented. 
 

 Others 

 
 Must be a current resident of the Philippines 

 Willing to work graveyard hours, 5 days a week, 9 hours a day (with a one-hour meal break) 

 Own a laptop or desktop 

 Have a valid government ID 

 Have an existing bank account or willing to open one if hired 

 Have a stable internet connection that is at least 25 mbps and have a back-up connection too 

 Live in area where there is stable power supply that is not interrupted by constant power outages 
 

 $500 - $500 a month 

 Join us in shaping the future of real estate 

 The real estate industry is in the midst of a seismic shift, and the future belongs to those who break new ground. As one of the fastest-growing companies in the proptech and marketing sectors, Luxury Presence challenges the status quo of what technology can do for real estate agents, leaders, and brokerages. 

 We’re a team of agile and tenacious innovators working collaboratively to drive the industry forward. Together, we build game-changing products that empower modern real estate entrepreneurs to dominate their markets. From award-winning web design to agile SEO solutions to cutting-edge AI tools, we deliver tech that anticipates market shifts and keeps our clients ahead of their competition. 

 Founded in 2016 by Stanford Business School alum Malte Kramer, Luxury Presence has grown to a global team ranked on the Inc. 5000 fastest-growing companies list three years in a row. We’re backed by world-class investors, including Bessemer Venture Partners, NextEquity Partners, Toba Capital, and Switch Ventures, and have raised $89 million to date. 

 More than 18,000 real estate businesses rely on our platform, including 30% of the Wall Street Journal RealTrends top agents and teams. Additionally, many of the industry’s most powerful brokerages rely on Luxury Presence as a trusted business partner. 

 Every year since 2020, Luxury Presence has ranked on BuiltIn’s Best Place to Work lists. HousingWire named our founder and CEO a 2024 Tech Trendsetter, we’ve received several Tech100 Awards, and we just scored an Inman Innovation Award for Best AI-Powered Platform. 

 Luxury Presence is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin. 

 Recruitment Notice: Luxury Presence employees will only contact candidates from an @luxurypresence.com email address. We may work with trusted recruiting partners who will contact you from their company’s email domain. If you have questions about the authenticity of a recruiting communication, please contact [email protected]. 

 We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

title: GTM Recruiter at Luxury Presence
description:
Luxury Presence is building the AI growth platform for real estate. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners and other top investors, we’re a Series C company that has hit $100M in annual recurring revenue. More than 90,000 real estate professionals, including over 30% of the WSJ Real Trends top 100 agents in the United States, use us to run and grow their business. 

 About the Role 

 Our Client Success org is the reason agents stay with Luxury Presence. Onboarding Specialists, Client Support Representatives, Client Success Managers, and Client Experience Specialists are the people our customers talk to every week, and we are hiring a lot of them in Scottsdale and Austin. 

 This is a junior recruiting seat with real ownership from day one. You will own our entry-level searches outright. Onboarding and Client Support reqs are yours from kickoff through offer: you source them, screen them, run the process, and close the candidate. 

 On Client Success and Client Experience searches, you’ll partner. You keep those funnels full with sourcing and screening while a senior recruiter carries the close. You get exposure to harder searches without being handed an offer conversation in your first recruiting job, and you take on the close once you have proven it on your own reqs. 

 If you want to learn full-cycle recruiting at a company hiring at pace, and you would rather be measured on real numbers than on effort, this is a strong place to start. 

 What You’ll Do 

 Own the entry-level searches 

 
 Run Onboarding and Client Support reqs full-cycle, from kickoff through offer.

 Run the intake with the hiring manager, set the bar, and hold it. 
 

 Partner on Client Success and Client Experience 

 
 Source and screen into those searches so the funnel never runs dry. 

 Hand a senior recruiter a slate they can work from, and stay close through the close. 

 Learn what separates a strong CSM or CX candidate from a strong entry-level one. 
 

 Sourcing 

 
 Find client-facing talent that does not come to us through inbound, using Boolean search, LinkedIn Recruiter, referrals, and local channels in Scottsdale and Austin. 

 Write outreach in your own voice, test what works, and keep the messages that earn replies. 

 Deliver 60 or more qualified sourced candidates a month across all the reqs you touch. 
 

 Screening 

 
 Run 15 to 20 candidate screens a week. 

 Screen against what each role actually requires. Work from the hiring manager’s intake and the scorecard, know what good looks like before you take the first call, and be able to defend why someone made the slate. 

 Submit a first slate of 5 to 6 approved candidates within 10 business days of every intake on your own reqs. 
 

 Candidate experience and process 

 
 Respond to every candidate within 24 hours and schedule the next step within 48 hours of a hiring manager decision. 

 Keep Lever current daily so anyone can see where a search stands. 

 Deliver a weekly pipeline snapshot to your hiring manager. 
 

 What We’re Looking For 

 Skills and Experience 

 
 0 to 2 years in recruiting, sourcing, or recruiting coordination. We will look just as hard at people coming from client success, support, onboarding, sales development, or hospitality who want to move into recruiting. 

 Comfort with high volume. You have held a role where the number of conversations you had each week was the point. 

 Clear, quick writing. You will send a lot of outreach and a lot of candidate updates. 

 Familiarity with an ATS or CRM. Lever experience helps and is not required. 

 No degree requirement. 
 

 Attributes 

 
 Coachable. You take direct feedback, apply it the same week, and ask for help early instead of quietly stalling. 

 Organized. You keep 20 or more candidates in flight without dropping anyone, using a system rather than memory. 

 Warm and direct. Candidates remember how you treated them, including the ones who do not get an offer.

 $70,000 - $80,000 a year 

 $70-80K base (DOE) plus bonus. This role is a hybrid setup in Scottsdale, AZ, or Austin, TX. 

 Join us in shaping the future of real estate

title: Senior Specialist, SEO at Moxie
description:
At Moxie, we empower ambitious aesthetic entrepreneurs to build profitable, independent practices—without burnout, overwhelm, or guesswork. In just a few years, we’ve grown from an idea to a global, remote-first team now supporting 700+ practices nationwide. 

 Our purpose is simple: to unlock sustainable success for aesthetic entrepreneurs, at every stage of their journey. 

 Senior SEO Specialist (IC3) 

 We’re looking for a Senior Specialist, SEO to own SEO as a strategic service line for hundreds of independent med spa practices — setting the strategy, raising and standardizing execution quality across our full book of practices, building the systems and reporting that let that quality scale without proportional headcount growth and leading a team of 2 SEO specialists who execute the day-to-day work across the practice book. 

 You’ll also be stepping into ground-floor ownership of how Moxie responds to the shift toward AI-driven search (GEO/AEO), defining our approach before most companies have figured theirs out. 

 SEO is one of Moxie’s highest-leverage, lowest-cost-per-lead channels, but today it’s delivered as a checklist of tactics, GBP hygiene, citations, on-page fixes, across our Enterprise, Gold, Silver, and Growth tiers, without a single owner. You’ll be that owner. You’ll sit within Marketing Services alongside paid media and website, report to our Marketing Services Lead, and partner closely with Provider Success, Product, Data, RevOps, and Sales. Getting this right compounds organic growth for practices at a fraction of paid-media cost, strengthens our Enterprise offering, and protects practices from local-search and AI-search shifts that could otherwise erode their visibility overnight. This role is US-based and remote. 

 Our objectives for the role 

 
 Turn SEO from ad hoc tactics into a standardized, repeatable system. In your first three months, audit a representative sample of practices (launcher, operator, Enterprise), ship 2–3 fast, visible fixes, and design the SEO playbook/SOP — with SLAs, QA checkpoints, and a reporting cadence. By month six, you own the recurring SEO motion (GBP management, citations, on-page and technical audits, reporting) as a system that runs consistently across the full book of practices. 

 Move the numbers and prove it. Measurably improve a core SEO metric — keyword ranking movement, Map Pack visibility, organic lead volume — across a defined cohort of practices by month six. By month nine, show defensible before/after growth in organic-channel contribution to lead volume and revenue across the practice book. 

 Build the systems that scale. Define a local SEO tool stack (rank tracking, citation management, reporting automation) in partnership with RevOps and Product, and get reporting and optimization running on a largely self-serve system — dashboards, automated alerts, standardized playbooks — that requires minimal manual, per-practice effort from the rest of Marketing Services. 

 Define Moxie’s answer to AI search. Test and document our approach to GEO/AEO visibility (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), and set a 12-month roadmap for how the SEO service evolves across local, technical, content, and AI-search components. 

 Be Moxie’s SEO voice. Become the recognized internal subject matter expert — mentoring others, informing sales conversations, supporting Enterprise SEO asks and the Marketing Audit & Action Plan (MAAP), and shaping the SEO piece of the Enterprise offering. 
 

 We’re looking for: 

 
 5+ years of hands-on SEO, ideally managing SEO across many small or local businesses simultaneously — at an agency or in-house at a multi-location brand — not just one brand. 

 Depth across all four pillars: technical SEO (site speed, schema/structured data, crawlability), on-page/content SEO, local SEO (GBP, citations, Map Pack), and emerging GEO/AEO. 

 Fluency with the standard stack: GA4, Google Search Console, SEMrush or Ahrefs, Screaming Frog, and a local-SEO/citation platform such as BrightLocal, Whitespark, or Yext. 

 A systems thinker, not just a practitioner. You’re energized by standardizing and scaling high-quality execution, reporting, and communication across hundreds of practices rather than hand-crafting one strategy at a time. 

 1-3+ years managing or mentoring junior team members, ideally in a marketing or SEO context. 

 Comfort owning a service line end to end: setting strategy, defining SLAs and QA, and reporting impact in business terms — leads and revenue — not just rankings and traffic. 

 Bonus: local-service, multi-location, or franchise SEO experience, given the parallels to Moxie’s hundreds-of-practices model. 
 

 Why Join us? 

 
 Above all, we’re in this to empower small business owners to own and grow their businesses. If you succeed, Med Spas will remain the opportunity for independent owner-operators instead of being dominated by a small number of large chains. If that speaks to you, speak to us. 

 We have much left to build. But given the market feedback we’re getting and our founding team’s company-building experience, we think we are writing the first chapters of a real success story. 

 Experience taking over as the owner of an entire service line. Most SEO roles go deep on one brand or spread thin across a few dozen clients; this one offers real strategy-setting authority plus the scale and data of hundreds of practices to test and prove what works. A role like this molds to its owner, but inevitably stretches and grows you as well. 

 Define how Moxie approaches the AI-search shift (GEO/AEO) before most companies have figured it out — and if you’ve been frustrated by shallow, checklist-driven SEO, build the systems and standards you’ve always wished existed. 

 Competitive salary and stock, and generous health/dental/vision coverage 
 

 At Moxie, we believe in creating a workplace where everyone feels valued, trusted, and included. Our team lives by our values: act as owners, give more than we take, move with speed and care, and simplify and learn every day. 

 We welcome people of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives to apply. If you require any accommodations to fully participate in the interview process, please let us know, we’re happy to assist.

title: Remote Electrical Estimator at Kimmel & Associates
description:
About the Company 

 Our client is a well-established engineering and consulting firm with decades of experience supporting complex infrastructure projects throughout the Mid-Atlantic and across the United States. The firm specializes in mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (M/E/P) estimating services for public and private sector clients, with expertise spanning water and wastewater treatment facilities, electric bus depots, transportation infrastructure, and other mission-critical projects. Known for its technical excellence and collaborative culture, the organization delivers reliable cost planning that supports informed decision-making throughout the project lifecycle. 

 About the Position 

 Our client is seeking an experienced Electrical Estimator to join its growing team. This role prepares detailed construction cost estimates at various stages of design development to support owner budgeting, capital planning, and procurement strategy. 

 Unlike traditional contractor estimating positions, this is not a hard-bid role. The focus is on developing accurate, comprehensive cost projections that help clients make informed decisions throughout planning and design. 

 The position is remote day to day, but it is not location-agnostic. Onboarding and training happen at the company’s office in Parkton, Maryland, and the team meets in person periodically. Candidates should live within reasonable driving distance of Parkton (greater Baltimore, York/Harrisburg, northern Maryland, southern Pennsylvania) or be open to relocating there. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 
 Prepare accurate electrical construction cost estimates from conceptual design through final construction documents. 
 Review construction drawings, specifications, and supporting documentation to develop detailed quantity takeoffs and pricing. 
 Evaluate labor, material, equipment, subcontractor, and installation costs. 
 Collaborate with engineering teams to clarify scope and identify potential cost impacts. 
 Support budgeting, value engineering, and cost planning throughout project development. 
 Maintain estimating documentation and contribute to improving estimating practices. 
 

 Requirements 

 
 5 to 10 years of electrical estimating experience, preferably within M/E/P, infrastructure, or industrial construction. 
 Strong understanding of electrical systems, construction drawings, specifications, and estimating methodologies. 
 Experience preparing estimates across multiple phases of design development. 
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and estimating software. Training is provided on the firm’s proprietary platform. 
 Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. 
 Self-motivated, with a track record of working independently in a remote setting. 
 Located within commuting distance of Parkton, Maryland, or willing to relocate. Occasional travel for training, team meetings, and project site visits. 
 

 Benefits 

 
 Remote work environment with flexible scheduling. 
 Impactful infrastructure and public works projects. 
 Collaborative team of experienced engineering and estimating professionals. 
 Training on the company’s estimating software and processes. 
 Professional growth and long-term career development. 
 Competitive compensation commensurate with experience. 
 Comprehensive benefits package, details provided during the interview process.

title: Product Designer, Growth Pricing & Revenue Systems at Gusto
description:
About Gusto 

 At Gusto, we’re on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve. 

 All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy. 

 AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process. 

 About Design at Gusto 

 Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We’re a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don’t care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. 

 We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We’re looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers. 

 About the Role 

 Gusto’s Growth team owns the full customer funnel — from a small business’s first visit to gusto.com through onboarding and into ongoing expansion. Two of the most complex, cross-cutting systems inside that funnel are how we price and package our products, and how we orchestrate the messages customers get across email, sales, and in-product surfaces. Neither has ever had dedicated, systems-level design support until now. 

 This role is leveled at the equivalent to a Staff-level. As Product Designer in this scope, you’ll own the design system for how promotions, tiers, and SKUs are presented consistently across the funnel, including a unified checkout experience, and drive the next wave of iteration following our fall pricing & packaging refresh. Alongside that, you’ll partner closely with our Revenue Systems team to define the target-state UX vision for customer-centric orchestration: establishing how a customer experiences one coordinated set of communications across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces, rather than a patchwork of independent touchpoints, and drawing the line between what belongs at the platform level versus the channel level. You’ll round this out with lighter-touch, ongoing design support for Invoicing & Billing as needs arise, including near-term work like multi-entity billing. 

 This is a systems-thinking role, with direct impact on revenue generation. You’ll need to be as comfortable zooming out to define a multi-team experience architecture as you are zooming in to get the details of a specific surface right, and you’ll need a strong customer experience and business sensibility to match. 

 About the team 

 Gusto’s Growth team is dedicated to helping customers discover, adopt, and expand into the Gusto ecosystem in meaningful ways. You’ll be joining a collaborative, cross-functional team of designers, engineers, PMs, data scientists, and key business partners who care deeply about customer experience — and who operate at the intersection of product-led growth, marketing, and sales. In this role, you’ll work closely with partners across Growth & Commerce, Revenue Systems, Sales, Marketing, and BizTech, while serving as the lead designer across several interrelated surfaces and systems. 

 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day: 

 
 Design dynamic pricing and packaging displays that span the funnel—from acquisition through activation and billing to ensure that buyers will quickly and confidently purchase Gusto products. 
 Design across Gusto’s invoicing and billing surfaces, building on the recently rebuilt IBEX platform 
 Build and improve internal tools such as the Promo Engine and Product Catalog, and improve existing workflows in Gusto’s internal platforms, to enable self-service and better outcomes for internal teams across Growth, Marketing, Accounting, Sales, and Expansion Sales. 
 Partner with Revenue Systems to define the target-state UX vision for multi-channel messaging orchestration—establishing systems cohesion across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces, and standardizing how AI-driven messaging is structured, sequenced, and represented to customers. 
 Draw the line between what belongs at the platform level versus the channel level (e.g., AI Email, Rec Center, Gus) so each surface stops solving the same problems separately. 
 Drive holistic service design, connecting the dots between how internal teams support customer decisions and how customers experience pricing, billing, and messaging throughout their journey. 
 Collaborate deeply with cross-functional partners to align on strategy, lead workshops, and co-create end-to-end solutions across multiple surfaces. 
 Create scalable, consistent patterns by working with and contributing to Gusto’s design system to ensure alignment across internal and external experiences. 
 Use a mix of data and qualitative insights to validate decisions, inform tradeoffs, and refine designs over time through iteration. 
 

 Here’s what we’re looking for: 

 
 8+ years of product design experience with a strong portfolio of systems-level design, internal tooling, and customer-facing product surfaces. 
 Experience working on complex, data-rich products—particularly in B2B SaaS environments with interconnected product offerings. 
 Demonstrated success in designing for both internal users and external customers, and the ability to balance their competing needs. 
 Fluency in UX best practices, UI design, interaction design, and accessibility standards. 
 Strong service design capabilities and a proven ability to map and simplify complex systems across touchpoints and orgs. 
 Experience designing for multi-channel systems cohesion—unifying messaging, sequencing, and experience across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces—and a point of view on standardizing AI-driven messaging at scale. 
 Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to lead through influence and align cross-functional teams. 
 Comfort leading ambiguous, 0-to-1 work, and building long-term vision while executing toward near-term milestones. 
 Experience using tools like Figma, Amplitude, and FullStory—and in leveraging mixed-methods research to inform design. 
 Passion for empowering internal teams and improving the quality of internal systems through intuitive, scalable design. 
 

 Our cash compensation range for this role is $147,000/yr to $183,000/yr in Denver, and $177,000/yr to $222,000/yr in San Francisco and New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above. 

 

 Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto’s subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale. 

 Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 

 When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees. 

 

 Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it’s the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. 

 Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

This is a senior individual contributor role with real ownership: you’ll author the AV standard that every site and every integrator builds against, own the multi-site capital roadmap, and design and direct the productions our executives and customers see. You’ll also serve as technical lead on our company-wide migration from Zoom to Google Meet, resetting a fleet of 200+ conference rooms in the process. If you’ve spent your career executing someone else’s drawings and are ready to own the drawing, this is that role. 

 About the Team 

 As a member of the AV Engineering team, you’ll sit within AIT Operations alongside the AIT Geeks, Inventory, Corporate Identity Engineering, Product AIT and Collaboration Tools. We’re a small, high-trust team that owns the technology Gusties touch every day, and we’re AI-forward — with a governed platform that gives engineers tools like Claude and Claude Code to automate the repetitive parts of the job. AV is the most visible surface we own: when a room works or an all-hands delivers, people notice. You’ll be the senior-most AV technical voice in the company and the SME for our AV platforms, partnering closely with Workplace, Networking, Client Platform Engineering, Brand, and Executive Operations. 

 Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day 

 
 Own AV design and programming — design, testing, troubleshooting, implementation of AV technology in Gusto’s offices, meeting spaces, and all hands event spaces across San Francisco, Denver, New York, Burlingame, and Scottsdale, with new sites in planning. Integrators move to install, labor, and specialist overflow rather than design lead. 
 Author and maintain the Gusto AV standard — room tiers, signal flow, control systems, camera and lighting standards, and the event production baseline that every site and vendor builds against. 
 Architect and own the technology and production for all of Gusto’s high-profile events — company-wide meetings (remote and in person), our flagship multi-day customer event, fireside chats, onsites, and podcast productions. You set the production design, spec and build the technical package, direct the show, and own the failure modes. 
 Lead the AV workstream of our Zoom to Google Meet migration — room interoperability, native Meet conversions, room hardware strategy, identity and policy mapping, and downstream integration dependencies. 
 Own the multi-site AV capital roadmap and vendor relationships , including vendor and project management of office buildouts and upgrades, negotiating investment and tradeoffs across sites and holding integrators and manufacturers accountable to design intent. 
 Administer our AV SaaS offerings — Google Meet and Zoom room fleets, Logitech and Neat endpoints, and streaming and event platforms — including room health monitoring, dashboards, and firmware lifecycle. 
 Act as the escalation path for the IT Geeks Support team for meeting space technology and events, and stay current with AV technology to ensure Gusto’s business needs are being met. 
 Use AI to automate the work that shouldn’t be manual — room health reporting, standards and runbook documentation, show-control logic, and vendor and RFP analysis. We expect you to build tooling, not just maintain spreadsheets. 
 Coach the team. Enable our IT Geeks team and event technicians to own tier-one AV and day-of production, support in-house video production projects, and document your domains so neither is a single point of failure. 
 

 Here’s what we’re looking for 

 
 8+ years of AV engineering experience , including time as the senior-most or design-owning AV resource for a multi-site organization. You’ve produced designs of record — room tiers, signal flow, rack elevations, control narratives — not just reviewed an integrator’s drawings. 
 Demonstrated technical direction of high-stakes live events. You’ve designed and called executive-fronted or external-facing shows end to end, including the failover plan for when something breaks mid-show. 
 Deep hands-on control, audio, and video systems expertise: AV control system programming (QSC strongly preferred; experience with Crestron, Biamp, and Extron a bonus), video switching and production (Barco E2, Ross Ultrix, Blackmagic ATEM), audio routing over IP networks such as Dante, comfort on an audio board with at least 16 channels including microphone systems and the ability to tune a room, theatrical and architectural lighting systems and fixtures (ETC, Paradigm, Martin, Chroma Q), and DMX networking. 
 Meeting-space and streaming platform depth: advanced knowledge of video collaboration offerings (Google Meet, Zoom Rooms, Neat, Logitech), meeting space technologies, acoustical design and lighting; video routing and signal flow across live event productions, digital signage networks, conference rooms, and virtual events; live streaming topology (P2P, AWS MediaLive and MediaConnect, encoding, Wirecast, vMix, OBS); PTZ and broadcast cameras with Sony Cinema Line familiarity; show programming (QLab, Stream Deck, Bitfocus Companion, OSC); post-production in DaVinci Resolve; and solid network architecture fundamentals as they apply to AV-over-IP. 
 AI fluency as a working practice. You use AI tools daily and can build with them — scripting control logic, generating documentation and runbooks, pulling and analyzing platform data via APIs. 
 Capital and vendor accountability. You’ve owned or materially driven an annual AV budget and a portfolio of integrator and manufacturer relationships, and you can articulate tradeoffs you personally negotiated. 
 The attributes that make this role work: a technology enthusiast always excited to learn new apps, devices, and better ways to do things; a passion for automation and highly efficient workflows; outstanding people and communication skills with the ability to influence without positional authority; calm under live-show pressure and willing to own failure modes; you love solving problems and getting at the root of issues; upbeat and positive, motivated by making someone else’s day smoother; super detail oriented and highly organized — it bothers you when things aren’t lined up properly or documentation doesn’t exist; incredibly reliable and you follow through on what you promise; and you proactively handle anticipated issues before they arise. This role is hands-on and San Francisco based, with travel to Gusto sites and event-hours flexibility.

The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto’s subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.
